title: 3D-Assisted Personalized Digital Patient Education Before Elective Lumbar Fusion: Effects on Decisional Conflict, Resilience, and PROMs in a Prospective Randomized Parallel-Group Study
summary:
Spinal conditions and degenerative changes are common causes of persistent back pain, limited mobility, and reduced quality of life. When surgery on the lower back is planned, patients often face a difficult decision: they need to understand and weigh the possible benefits, risks, pain, recovery time, and expectations regarding the outcome. This situation can be stressful and may lead to uncertainty.
This study investigates whether clearer patient education using a personalized digital 3D model can better support patients before a planned lower back fusion surgery. It examines whether patients feel more confident in their decision, understand the treatment better, and are mentally better prepared for surgery after this type of explanation. The study also looks at whether this improved preparation later affects pain, mobility, quality of life, and return to everyday activities. It compares standard patient education with an additional visual 3D presentation of the patient’s own spine. The aim is to find out whether better explanation before surgery can reduce uncertainty and positively influence recovery over time.
conditions: Osteochondrosis of the spine in adults: lumbar region

interventions.name: In Arm 1, patients receive standardized, script-based preoperative patient education before elective posterior lumbar fusion. In addition to conventional patient education, a patient-specific digital 3D model of the lumbar spine is used, based on the patient’s already available clinical imaging data

In the control group, patients receive standardized, script-based preoperative patient education before elective posterior lumbar fusion. The content and duration of the patient education are identical to those in the intervention group and include an explanation of the individual clinical findings,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned elective posterior lumbar spinal fusion involving 1 or 2 segments
Sufficient German language skills to participate in patient education and questionnaire assessments
Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Emergency hospital admission or urgent surgery
Infectious cause of the spinal disorder
Tumor-related indication, including primary or secondary tumor disease or spinal metastases
Previous lumbar spinal fusion surgery
